**Fix:** make sure `/etc/app/app.conf` is put on target instances before this runbook runs, either when the instance is built or as a step earlier in the runbook. ## Results
I've written a fix plan, but you can't run it as-is. Everything from the failed run is gone: the instance (`i-00000000000000001_47`), the `ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-*` runbooks and their automation role no longer exist. So the plan is for the next run and uses placeholders you'll need to fill in. Nothing has been executed. The plan passed the safe-deployment policy check with no violations.

**What happened.** The execution ID you gave (`0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab`) doesn't exist in SSM, and there's no document named exactly `ReleaseOrchestrator`. The fix is based on the `ssm-baseline-m4-*-ReleaseOrchestrator` runbooks in account `012345678901_1`, `us-east-1`. All 9 recorded runs (2026-11-04 to 2026-11-25) failed the same way. The child runbook's `ApplyConfig` step exits with code 3 when `/etc/app/app.conf` is missing on the target instance, and the parent runbook then fails. The runbook, the IAM role and the SSM agent connection all worked. We don't know why the file was missing.

**What I found in the account today:**
- No `ssm-baseline-m4*` runbooks exist.
- No `ssm-baseline*` CloudFormation stacks are listed, not even deleted ones.
- The role `ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-automation` returns `NoSuchEntity`.
- The only running EC2 instances belong to the `obsgap-poc-workload` stack.
- The 3 SSM hybrid nodes (`mi-…`) all show `ConnectionLost`.

There's no live target right now, and I didn't assume one of the running instances is it.

**The fix:** put `/etc/app/app.conf` on the target instance before running ReleaseOrchestrator, then run it again. Make this permanent in the provisioning code (see the end).

## Placeholders to fill in
- `<STACK_PREFIX>`: the prefix of the redeployed runbook set, e.g. `ssm-baseline-m4-r4-a1`.
- `<TARGET_INSTANCE_ID>`: the instance the run will target.
- `<CONFIG_SOURCE>`: wherever your approved `app.conf` lives, e.g. `s3://<CONFIG_BUCKET>/<CONFIG_KEY>`. I couldn't find this in the account.

## Execution plan

**1. Prepare**
```
aws ssm describe-document --name <STACK_PREFIX>-ApplyAppConfig --region us-east-1 --query 'Document.[Name,DocumentVersion,Status]'
aws ssm describe-document --name <STACK_PREFIX>-ReleaseOrchestrator --region us-east-1 --query 'Document.[Name,DocumentVersion,Status]'
aws iam get-role --role-name <STACK_PREFIX>-automation --query 'Role.Arn'
```
- This confirms the redeployed runbooks and their automation role exist, and records their versions as your baseline. Today all three are absent, so redeploy the stack first.

**2. Pre-validate**
```
aws ssm describe-instance-information --region us-east-1 --filters Key=InstanceIds,Values=<TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --query 'InstanceInformationList[].[InstanceId,PingStatus,PlatformName]'
```
- Continue only if `PingStatus` is `Online`.

```
aws ssm send-command --region us-east-1 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --instance-ids <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --parameters 'commands=["ls -l /etc/app/app.conf || echo MISSING"]' --query 'Command.CommandId' --output text
aws ssm get-command-invocation --region us-east-1 --command-id <CMD_ID> --instance-id <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --query '[Status,StandardOutputContent]'
```
- This only reads. If the output is `MISSING`, go to Apply. If the file is already there, skip to the re-run.

**3. Apply**
```
aws ssm send-command --region us-east-1 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --instance-ids <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --parameters 'commands=["set -e","sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/app","if [ ! -f /etc/app/app.conf ]; then sudo aws s3 cp <CONFIG_SOURCE> /etc/app/app.conf && echo CREATED_BY_MITIGATION; fi","sudo chmod 0644 /etc/app/app.conf","ls -l /etc/app/app.conf"]' --query 'Command.CommandId' --output text
aws ssm get-command-invocation --region us-east-1 --command-id <CMD_ID> --instance-id <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --query '[Status,StandardOutputContent,StandardErrorContent]'
```
- This creates the file only if it's missing and never overwrites an existing one.
- **Risk:** the instance profile needs `s3:GetObject` on the config source. If you don't have an approved source, place the file with your usual configuration tool instead.
- **Note:** if the output says `CREATED_BY_MITIGATION`, write it down; Rollback depends on it.

```
aws ssm start-automation-execution --region us-east-1 --document-name <STACK_PREFIX>-ReleaseOrchestrator --parameters 'AutomationAssumeRole=[redacted ARN]<STACK_PREFIX>-automation,InstanceId=<TARGET_INSTANCE_ID>' --query AutomationExecutionId --output text
```
- This re-runs the orchestrator. Record the `AutomationExecutionId` it returns.

**4. Post-validate**
```
aws ssm get-automation-execution --region us-east-1 --automation-execution-id <NEW_EXECUTION_ID> --query 'AutomationExecution.[AutomationExecutionStatus,StepExecutions[].[StepName,StepStatus,Outputs]]'
aws ssm describe-automation-executions --region us-east-1 --filters Key=ParentExecutionId,Values=<NEW_EXECUTION_ID> --query 'AutomationExecutionMetadataList[].[AutomationExecutionId,DocumentName,AutomationExecutionStatus]'
```
- Expected: the parent's `Prepare` and `RunApplyConfig` steps show `Success`, and the child `ApplyAppConfig` / `ApplyConfig` run shows `Success`, with no "config file /etc/app/app.conf missing" error.

**5. Rollback** (only if Apply created the file and it causes problems)
```
aws ssm send-command --region us-east-1 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --instance-ids <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --parameters 'commands=["sudo mv /etc/app/app.conf /etc/app/app.conf.rolledback.$(date +%s)"]'
```
- This moves the file aside rather than deleting it, so it can be restored.
- **Note:** run it only if Apply printed `CREATED_BY_MITIGATION`. Moving a file that was already there could break the app.
- **Note:** after rollback, ReleaseOrchestrator will fail with exit code 3 again until the file is restored.

## Permanent fix (provisioning code)
I didn't find a repository URL, so this is a requirement rather than a specific change.

1. **Create the file when the instance is built.** Add creation of `/etc/app/app.conf` to the provisioning (launch template user data, AMI build, or a State Manager association). A newly launched target should already have the file before ReleaseOrchestrator runs.
2. **Fail fast in the runbook.** Optionally add an `aws:assertAwsResourceProperty` or `aws:runCommand` check to the ReleaseOrchestrator template before `RunApplyConfig`. If the file is missing, it should stop with a clear "provisioning incomplete" message. Running it against an unprovisioned instance should fail at that check, not at `ApplyConfig`.
3. **Keep the stack's resources together.** Ensure the stack that creates the instance and the one that creates the runbooks are ordered, or are one stack. The run should only start once the instance's `app.conf` setup has finished.

## What this doesn't cover
- **Why the file was missing.** Neither the investigation nor my reads confirmed it, so the permanent fix covers the likely gap: the file was never created when the instance was built.
- **Your execution ID.** I couldn't link it to anything in this account and region. If it came from a different account or region, check there.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Put /etc/app/app.conf on the target instance before re-running ReleaseOrchestrator, and make provisioning create it

## Reasoning
All 9 recorded runs failed because the ApplyConfig guard exits 3 when /etc/app/app.conf is missing. The original instance, runbooks and automation role no longer exist, so this plan is for the next run and uses placeholders: <STACK_PREFIX> (e.g. ssm-baseline-m4-r4-a1), <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID>, <CONFIG_SOURCE> (e.g. s3://<CONFIG_BUCKET>/<CONFIG_KEY>). Passed the safe-deployment policy check; nothing executed.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Verify the runbooks and automation role exist and record their versions…
**Type:** command
```
aws ssm describe-document --name <STACK_PREFIX>-ApplyAppConfig --region us-east-1 --query 'Document.[Name,DocumentVersion,Status]'
aws ssm describe-document --name <STACK_PREFIX>-ReleaseOrchestrator --region us-east-1 --query 'Document.[Name,DocumentVersion,Status]'
aws iam get-role --role-name <STACK_PREFIX>-automation --query 'Role.Arn'
```
**Purpose:** Verify the runbooks and automation role exist and record their versions as a baseline.
**Advisory:** All three are absent today; redeploy the stack first.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Confirm the target is reachable; continue only if PingStatus is Online
**Type:** command
```
aws ssm describe-instance-information --region us-east-1 --filters Key=InstanceIds,Values=<TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --query 'InstanceInformationList[].[InstanceId,PingStatus,PlatformName]'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the target is reachable; continue only if PingStatus is Online.

#### 2.2 Check read-only whether app.conf is present; if MISSING go to Apply…
**Type:** command
```
aws ssm send-command --region us-east-1 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --instance-ids <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --parameters 'commands=["ls -l /etc/app/app.conf || echo MISSING"]' --query 'Command.CommandId' --output text
aws ssm get-command-invocation --region us-east-1 --command-id <CMD_ID> --instance-id <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --query '[Status,StandardOutputContent]'
```
**Purpose:** Check read-only whether app.conf is present; if MISSING go to Apply, otherwise skip to the re-run.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Create app.conf only if missing, never overwriting an existing file
**Type:** command
```
aws ssm send-command --region us-east-1 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --instance-ids <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --parameters 'commands=["set -e","sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/app","if [ ! -f /etc/app/app.conf ]; then sudo aws s3 cp <CONFIG_SOURCE> /etc/app/app.conf && echo CREATED_BY_MITIGATION; fi","sudo chmod 0644 /etc/app/app.conf","ls -l /etc/app/app.conf"]' --query 'Command.CommandId' --output text
aws ssm get-command-invocation --region us-east-1 --command-id <CMD_ID> --instance-id <TARGET_INSTANCE_ID> --query '[Status,StandardOutputContent,StandardErrorContent]'
```
**Purpose:** Create app.conf only if missing, never overwriting an existing file.
**Risks:** Instance profile needs s3:GetObject on the config source; without an approved source, place the file with your usual configuration tool.
**Advisory:** Note whether the output says CREATED_BY_MITIGATION; Rollback depends on it.

#### 3.2 Re-run the orchestrator and record the new AutomationExecutionId
**Type:** command
```
aws ssm start-automation-execution --region us-east-1 --document-name <STACK_PREFIX>-ReleaseOrchestrator --parameters 'AutomationAssumeRole=[redacted ARN]<STACK_PREFIX>-automation,InstanceId=<TARGET_INSTANCE_ID>' --query AutomationExecutionId --output text
```
**Purpose:** Re-run the orchestrator and record the new AutomationExecutionId.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Verify Prepare, RunApplyConfig and the child ApplyConfig all show…
**Type:** command

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### ssm-baseline-m4-*-ReleaseOrchestrator runs all fail
**Description:** In account 012345678901_1 / us-east-1, all ssm-baseline-m4-*-ReleaseOrchestrator runs on record (2026-11-04 to 2026-11-25) failed at RunApplyConfig (aws:executeAutomation), because the child ApplyAppConfig step ApplyConfig exits 3. No successful run was found. The execution ID the user gave (0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab) does not exist.
**Time:** 2026-11-04T01:30:43Z - 2026-11-25T07:18:52Z

## Findings

### Cause: /etc/app/app.conf is missing on the target instance
**Description:** ApplyAppConfig's run-command script exits 3 when /etc/app/app.conf doesn't exist. On i-00000000000000001_47 it hits that guard every time, so the child automation fails and ReleaseOrchestrator fails with it. The same error appears in every ReleaseOrchestrator run since 2026-11-04. It is not yet known why the file is missing: never provisioned, removed, or a wrong path.
**Cascades to:** symptom-releaseorchestrator-failures

#### Supporting Observations
- **Latest run 5f5732bd: ApplyConfig guard exits 3 on i-00000000000000001_47:** Parent ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-ReleaseOrchestrator (5f5732bd, 2026-11-25 07:18:43Z) ran two steps. Step Prepare (aws:sleep PT5S) succeeded. Step RunApplyConfig (aws:executeAutomation) failed: it ran child ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-ApplyAppConfig (c40fd382) with role ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-automation on instance i-00000000000000001_47.

The child's ApplyConfig step (aws:runCommand with AWS-RunShellScript, command 34938b01) ran on i-00000000000000001_47 (ip-10-0-0-6.ec2.internal). The script starts with a guard, `if [ ! -f /etc/app/app.conf ]; then ... exit 3; fi`, which fired in under a second with ResponseCode 3. The failure is the script's own deliberate pre-check, not an SSM agent or permissions problem. Command output is not sent to S3 or CloudWatch.
- **Every ReleaseOrchestrator run failed: /etc/app/app.conf missing:** The orchestrator documents in this account are named with a stack prefix (ssm-baseline-m4-*-ReleaseOrchestrator). There is no document called just ReleaseOrchestrator. All 10 failed ReleaseOrchestrator executions found failed the same way. In each, the child ApplyAppConfig automation's Run Command step exited with code 3: `applying release configuration — ERROR: config file /etc/app/app.conf missing`. The parent then fails because the child automation failed.

Runs:
- 2026-11-25 07:18:43Z: 5f5732bd (m4-r3-a14), child c40fd382
- 2026-11-25 05:34:09Z: cdd22328 (m4-r2-a14), child 57004db8

None of these is execution 0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab, and that execution has no child executions.

#### Gaps
- **Why app.conf was never provisioned is unknown:** Instance i-00000000000000001_47 no longer exists. The m4-r3-a14 runbooks and the IAM role ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-automation were removed in CloudFormation stack cleanup (07:21–07:22Z), so how the instance was provisioned could not be inspected.
